column1: # Output-flag worklist -- RESIDUAL after the 2026-07 output-flag write sweep. The 150 real
# write-path flags are now gated (pathgates.toml [roles.X]); these ~65 rows are the VERIFIED
# format-only / non-path flags that harmlessly auto-approve (an output FORMAT like `-o json`, a
# column list, a GHC option, a boolean, or a non-existent flag -- the tool errors or ignores, it
# every output-flag hole must be listed here (a NEW one fails closed => a real writer to gate), and
# a listed entry that stops auto-approving fails as stale. The list only shrinks. Format: <cmd>\t<flag>
# ── TRIAGED 2026-08-08 (a–f slice of the 2026-08-07 seeding) — verified NON-PATH values ─────────
# Each row below was checked against the tool's own reference for the researched version. The value
# the flag takes is an ENUM, an identifier, or a JSON blob — never a filesystem path — so a path
# there is a nonsense value and no write occurs. Recorded per command:
#   argocd version --output          `wide|json|yaml|name` — the Argo CD global output format.
#                                    are the path flags, and they are not in the allowlist.)
#   clever … -o                      `-o` is the short form of `--org` on every clever sub — an
#                                    organisation id/name routed to the API, not a local path.
#                                    (`clever`'s own path flags are on other subs.)
#   code --add-mcp                   a JSON server definition passed inline, e.g. `{"name":…}`.
#   code --install-extension         an extension identifier, or a `.vsix` to READ. Either way it
#                                    is an input, never a write target; the write lands in the
#                                    extensions dir, which is what put it in `write_flags`.
#                                    `json|text` — the format the signature payload is printed in.
#                                    (`--output-file` is cosign's path flag; not in the allowlist.)
#   dart format -o/--output          `write|show|json|none` — WHERE formatted output goes, as an
#                                    enum. See the note in the untriaged block: dart format's
#                                    positional rewrite is a separate, still-open question.
#   dbt {list,ls} --output           `name|path|selector|json` — the shape of the node listing.
# ── TRIAGED 2026-08-08 (q–s slice of the 2026-08-07 seeding) — verified NON-PATH values ──────────

# version in its `researched_version`, and the flag's value turned out to be an enum, a template, a
# boolean, or a `true`/`false` word — never a filesystem path.
#                                    `human|json` — the report NOTATION. Every write subcommand

#                                    files"). The probe path lands on the file-to-preview
#                                    positional, which is an INPUT; the thumbnail's destination is

#                                    directories these act on are positionals, and the
#                                    `rdfind_mode` handler already write-gates them once an action

# SECOND value and which no flag→role map can reach; neither safety sub takes a path positional

#                              target is the FILE positional, and it is already gated — the

# The seeded backlog is EMPTY: every row of it has been triaged and moved above, and every row that
# turned out to be a genuine writer was gated and deleted from this file. What remains in this file
# is entirely VERIFIED format-only / probe-artifact rows. A new row appearing below this header
# means the guard found something nobody has looked at yet.
# The history is kept because it explains what the counts mean and why the file is shaped this way.
# The guard used to derive its flag list from a hardcoded NAME list over `cmd.valued`, on top-level
# commands only. Three blind spots followed: `-i`/`-w`/`--in-place`/`--fix` were not on the name list
# (the in-place formatters — the largest writer family in the tree), `write_flags` was never read at
# all, and SUBS were never walked (which is why `vegeta report --output ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` was
# missed). Widening it on all three axes took the reported set from 62 to 424.
# These 362 are seeded so the ratchet HOLDS THE LINE at today's exposure — nothing new can ship
# ungated — rather than leaving the guard red and therefore ignored. They are a BURN-DOWN LIST, not
# an acknowledgement. Expect roughly three populations:
#     write to /etc/hosts or ~/.ssh — CONFIRMED by hand. These need a `[command.path_gate]`.
#   - format flags: `bazel query --output`, `argocd version --output` take `json`/`proto`, so a path
#     is a nonsense value and no write occurs. These belong above the line, with the check recorded.
#   - not-a-path-at-all: `borg check --repair`, `borg config --delete` swallowed the probe path as a
#     positional. A different question, and not this guard's.
# Triage order: the credential-touching ones first (`~/.ssh` reachable), then /etc, then the rest.
# a–f slice triaged 2026-08-08. The genuine writers are GATED and gone from this file (afhash -w,
# ameba --fix, ansible-vault encrypt --output, artillery report -o/--output, buf build/convert/
# format/generate -o/--output + format -w/--write, bun build --outdir, bundler-audit check --output,
# cdk synth -o/--output, coverage json -o, crystal build -o + docs --output, dawn scan -O/--output,
# dotnet-trace convert -o/--output, dvc add -o/--out, flutter analyze --write). The format-only ones
# moved above the line. What remains here from a–f are the three PROBE ARTIFACTS below: the flag is a
# BOOLEAN, so the probe's path never reaches it — it lands on a positional whose role is a different
# question than this guard asks, and gating it here would gate the wrong thing.
#   borg check --repair    boolean. `borg check [options] REPOSITORY_OR_ARCHIVE` — the probe path is
#                          swallowed as the repository spec, which --repair rebuilds in place. Not a
#   borg config --delete   boolean. `borg config REPOSITORY NAME` — the probe path is the repository
#   depcruise --init       boolean (optional `oneshot` word). It writes `.dependency-cruiser.js` into
#                          the CWD; the probe path is swallowed as a source directory to SCAN.
